2607.00415.title: A Mechanistic View of Authority Hierarchy in LLM Sycophancy
2607.00415.paper_summary: Authority bias poses a critical safety concern in language models: models systematically prioritize social cues from authority figures over factual consistency, swaying their answers based on source credibility rather than evidence. We mechanistically investigate this phenomenon using a controlled medical QA setting, where hints suggesting incorrect answers are attributed to personas of varying expertise. Across Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-2-9B, we find that models respond in a graded manner proportional to perceived authority, a hierarchy that is never explicitly prompted but emerges from training. Logit lens analysis and linear/non-linear probing localize this effect to a critical late layer where correct answer representations are actively erased, an erasure that scales with authority level, resists mean vector intervention, and is only partially reversible through chain-of-thought reasoning. Our findings suggest that authority-induced sycophancy is not a surface-level output bias but mechanistic knowledge erasure, a precise, layer-localized overwriting of correct internal representations by high-status authority signals.
2607.00415.paper_summary_zh: 權威偏見在語言模型中構成了一個關鍵的安全問題：模型系統性地優先考慮來自權威人物的社會線索，而非事實的一致性，根據來源的可信度而非證據來影響其回答。 我們在一個受控的醫療問答環境中機械性地調查這一現象，在這裡，暗示不正確答案的提示被歸因於不同專業水平的人物。 在 Llama-3.1-8B、Qwen3-8B 和 Gemma-2-9B 中，我們發現模型對感知的權威以比例方式作出反應，這種層級從未明確提示，但從訓練中浮現出來。 Logit lens 分析和線性/非線性探測將這一效應定位於一個關鍵的後期層，在這裡，正確答案的表示被主動抹去，這種抹去隨著權威水平的提高而擴大，抵抗均值向量的干預，並且僅能通過思維鏈推理部分可逆。我們的研究結果表明，權威引發的拍馬屁行為並不是一種表面層的輸出偏見，而是機械性知識的抹去，這是一種精確的、層級定位的高狀態權威信號對正確內部表示的覆寫。
